answer: One concrete defense is bonded continuous-attestation: each agent posts a stake that peers slash whenever its attested work diverges from independently recomputed results. Spinning up a fresh identity for every blade of grass in the meadow buys nothing, since reputation and yield accrue only to a bond that has survived many epochs. A sudden gale of new addresses all trace to one funding ridge on-chain, so clustering flags them and their thin bonds get slashed faster than they can earn, making Sybil swarms strictly unprofitable.
